articles.title: How the console is laid out
articles.sum: Every award edition, event and giving partner is a place with its own menu. You go in, work, and come back out.
blocks: The console has one menu at the top level and a separate menu for each thing you can open. Opening Teachers Prize, 4th Edition swaps the menu for that edition’s own pages: Overview, Nominations, Judging and so on. The name at the top of the menu is the switcher; Back brings you out.
Go into a thing and stay a while
An edition, an event, a partner, Settings
See another one of the same kind
See another view of the same thing
A nomination, a payment, a request
Type “refunds” or an old page name
⌘K opens Find. Enter opens the first match.
⌘J opens Ask, which answers from the place you’re in and this handbook.
Alt [ and Alt ] switch to the previous or next edition or event without opening the switcher.
Alt ↑ goes back. Esc closes any drawer.

Switching keeps your page. If you’re on Judging in the 4th Edition and switch to the 3rd, you land on the 3rd Edition’s Judging. If that page doesn’t exist there yet, you land on Overview and a line tells you why.
A number beside a menu item is work waiting on a person. Red means it affects production right now; amber means it may. A menu item with nothing waiting shows no number at all, never a 0.

articles.title: Your role and what it reaches
articles.sum: Access is given per page and, for event and award staff, per event or award. Every scoped access has an end date.
blocks: Everything, including configuration, keys and roles.
Content and programmes. Can draft a shortlist, can’t publish it.
Moderation and nomination review, limited to the awards they’re given.
One or more events, until the day after each one. Spends up to their limit; above it they ask.
The pages of one event their lead gives them, until the day after it.
The menu never offers a page your role can’t open. If you can see it, you can use it.
Volunteers and judges never sign in to this console. They have their own areas.
If you need a page you can’t see, ask the person who gave you access. Event leads use Requests › Access for my team, which goes to an admin with a reason and an end date.
Never share a sign-in. Everything you do is logged under your name, including notes you add when you act.

articles.title: Your first week
articles.sum: What to do on days one to five so you know where things are before something goes wrong.
blocks: Settings › Security and sign-in. Console roles sign in with a passkey.
Read How the console is laid out
Four minutes. Then press ⌘K and find three pages by typing.
Open one edition and one event
Walk their menus. Look at Overview and Today: they tell you what needs a person.
Read the playbook for your area
Moderators: Reviewing nominations. Event leads: Planning an event. Finance: Reconciling payments.
Sit with someone while they approve a refund or a nomination, and read the audit entry it leaves.
Home is sorted by consequence, not by date. Start every day at the top of it.

articles.title: Awards, editions and categories
articles.sum: An award runs in editions. Each edition has its own categories, dates, rules and terms. The overall winner of an edition is shown first on results.
blocks: Teachers Prize is the award. The 4th Edition is one run of it, with dates from nominations to the ceremony. Categories belong to the edition, so the 4th can add Rural teacher without changing the 3rd.
The public nominates. A person approves each nomination.
Finalists are chosen per category from approved nominations.
Free votes and optional contributions. Some editions are judging only.
Panels score finalists on the rubric. Judging happens after voting.
Results stay sealed until released, usually at the ceremony cue.
Judging happens after voting closes, never during it.
On results, the overall edition winner is shown first, then each category.
An edition can end in one event, or several editions can share one night. The event reads the edition’s dates as locked milestones.

articles.title: Setting up an edition
articles.sum: Nine steps from a blank edition to nominations open. Changes after opening publish as a new version.
blocks: Name, edition number, scope (state or LGA), and who runs it.
Six milestones: nominations open and close, shortlist, voting window, judging close, ceremony.
Pick an identity family and a cover. Looks are presets; there are no custom colours.
Name, who it’s for, and the minimum nominations before it can be shortlisted.
System fields are locked. Add evidence and region fields as needed.
Categories per nomination (1 to 3), reason length, self-nomination, daily limit per person.
Free only, or free plus contribution tiers with a cap per person per category.
Panels, rubric criteria and weights. Weights lock when nominations open.
Eligibility, prize and terms. Nominators accept the version that was live when they submitted.
Rubric weights and voting mode lock at open. Decide them before you press Open nominations.
Publishing a form or terms change creates a new version. Every nomination keeps the version it was submitted on.
An edition with steps left shows them as its Overview, so anyone can see what’s missing.

articles.title: Reviewing nominations
articles.sum: A person approves every nomination. Volunteer checks and platform checks are recommendations; you decide.
blocks: Review works oldest first. The desk shows one nomination at a time with the reason, the evidence, the platform’s checks, any volunteer recommendation with their name, and possible duplicates.
Read the reason against the category
Does the reason describe what the category rewards? If it fits another category better, say so.
Links open in a new tab. Files are scanned before you see them.
A volunteer flag is a recommendation, not a decision. Agree or disagree and say why.
Same name and school, or same phone, shows as a possible match. Compare before merging.
Approve, Return to the nominator with what to fix, or Reject with a reason from the list.
It fits the category and the rules.
Your note and a link to fix it
Ineligible, abusive, or a duplicate you merged.
Every nomination is approved by a person. Nothing is approved automatically.
The category-fit assistant is shown to admins and judges only. It is never mentioned in public.
Never contact a nominee or nominator from your own phone or email. Use the platform so it’s logged.
Volunteer agreement is sampled: 1 in 5 of their checks is compared with your decision. A note explaining a disagreement helps them improve.

articles.title: Duplicates and merging
articles.sum: When two nominations are the same person, merge them so votes and evidence land in one place.
blocks: Name, school, LGA, phone and photo.
Usually the older one, or the one with consent confirmed.
Reasons and evidence from both are kept. Nominators of both are told.
A merge can be undone for 24 hours from the audit entry. After that, ask an admin.
Volunteers can flag a possible duplicate. They can never merge.

articles.title: Shortlisting
articles.sum: Drafts are built from approved nominations and the scoring rule. Publishing needs an admin.
blocks: Draft shortlist builds a proposal per category. A category below its minimum nominations shows Too few and can’t be published until it reaches it or the minimum is changed in setup.
Publishing a shortlist needs an admin. Editors and moderators can prepare drafts.
Publishing sends the finalist letter, which includes how voting works. Check the letter before you publish.

articles.title: Judging: panels, conflicts and quorum
articles.sum: Panels score finalists on the edition’s rubric after voting closes. Conflicts exclude a judge from that category.
blocks: They sign in to the judges’ area, never the console.
A declared conflict excludes the judge from that category automatically.
After voting closes. Each judge scores every finalist in their panel.
Each category needs at least 3 complete scorecards.
Scores combine with votes using the edition’s weights.
A rubric criterion that has been used is retired, never deleted.
Volunteers never see scores or judges’ notes.

articles.title: How voting works
articles.sum: One free vote per verified person per category, plus optional contributions. Never shopping language.
blocks: Each person verifies with an email code and gets one free vote per category. Name, phone, email and a message are required; the name shown publicly is optional.
Editions in contribution mode offer tiers (from ₦100). A contribution adds votes and is capped per person per category. The person gets a receipt by email.
The collusion scan runs every hour during voting. Clusters it finds are held from the tally until a person looks.
Live totals and the race are public.
A paid vote that didn’t land is recovered once, from Money › Payments › Vote recovery, and logged.
Voting is never described in shopping language, anywhere.

articles.title: Releasing results
articles.sum: Results are sealed until one act releases them. Tie it to the ceremony cue so the page, emails and the hall screen change together.
blocks: Release is unavailable until every category has quorum.
See the results page as the public will. The overall winner comes first.
Now, a time, or the ceremony cue in the event’s run of show.
One act. The seal’s hash is recorded and verified on Data and audit › Integrity.
A release can’t be undone. A correction is a new, logged release with a reason shown publicly.
Badges, certificates and the legacy vault entry are issued automatically at release.

articles.title: Planning an event
articles.sum: An event is a place with its own team, work, money and night. Today tells you what blocks it.
blocks: Readiness is the share of work items done, weighted by how much each blocks the night. Today shows the items blocking it, the budget forecast and tickets.
Type an item as a sentence: “Book 3 marshals by Fri, Kemi, ₦45,000”. The owner, due date and budget are read from it. Every item has one owner.
Their dates become locked milestones in your timeline.
Event settings › Members. Access ends the day after the event.
Work, timeline, risks and decisions. Start from a template if one fits.
Finance sets the budget; you forecast against it.
Dates that come from an award are locked in the event. They change only in that award’s setup.
Write decisions down in Plan › Decisions with who and why. Next year’s lead will thank you.

articles.title: Budgets, limits and requests
articles.sum: A lead approves spending up to their limit. Anything above it is a request to finance, with what it does to the budget.
blocks: A spend request; the forecast turns red
What you need, the amount, when it’s needed, and what happens if it waits.
It names who decides and how long it usually takes.
It appears in your Requests and in the decider’s Waiting on you.
Read If approved: it shows the budget effect before you decide.
Approve, Ask for info, or Decline. Asking or declining needs a note; the person sees it.
Over-limit spending is never a dead end. The lead can always ask.
Finance is told at 80% of an event’s budget and again when the forecast passes 100%.

articles.title: Requests: asking and deciding
articles.sum: Anyone who can’t do something themselves asks. Each request has one decider, a usual time, and a trail.
blocks: Approve, ask for info or decline
The requester adds info, or withdraws
Not this time, with a reason
Asking for info and declining always need a note.
A request waiting more than a day turns amber on the decider’s Home.

articles.title: Running the door
articles.sum: Scanners hold an offline list, so the door works without signal. Red passes go to the gate lead, never back to the queue.
blocks: Event settings › Devices. Open /door on the phone and scan the code.
Each scanner downloads every valid pass. Check ‘Offline list loaded’.
Scan every pass; never let someone in by eye. Count the queue every 30 minutes.
The target is 0. A lost scan means someone got in without a record.
Unpairing wipes the list from the phone.
A steward never decides a red pass. It goes to the gate lead, who can check the name and the payment.
Volunteer hours at the door come from check-in and check-out scans. Nobody has to log them.

articles.title: The night: run of show
articles.sum: Cues in order, each with an owner. The results release can be tied to a cue.
blocks: Every cue has a time, what happens, who calls it and what’s on the hall screen. Sponsors’ logos run between cues as agreed in their benefits.
Lock the cue sheet 48 hours before
Changes after that go through the lead.
The page, the emails and the screen change together at that cue.
Keep the radio channels on the sheet
Results are released at the cue, not before dinner.

articles.title: After the night
articles.sum: The survey, locked hours and the report, on fixed days.
blocks: Guest survey goes out. Event access for the team ends.
Volunteer hours lock from door scans.
The final report: against budget, against last edition, decisions to keep.
Growth compares this edition with the last on the same day before the night, so you can see the trend while there’s still time to act.

articles.title: Reconciling payments
articles.sum: When the gateway took money and we recorded nothing, fix it before the person pays again.
blocks: Gateway check lists every payment where the gateway and our records disagree. The usual cause is a webhook that answered but didn’t write.
Each row shows the gateway reference, the amount, and what’s missing: a vote, a ticket or a receipt.
This creates what was paid for, exactly once, and sends the receipt.
Settings › Webhooks. If calls answer 200 but nothing is written, raise an incident.
Support tickets linked to the payment show on the same row.
Never refund and reconcile the same payment. Reconcile first; refund only if the person asks.
A payment that affects production shows red on the bell and on Home until it’s reconciled.

articles.title: Refunds and disputes
articles.sum: Decide refunds within two working days. Answer card disputes before the bank’s deadline.
blocks: Ticket, can’t attend, more than 48 h before
Offer a transfer to someone else
No refund once votes are counted, except duplicates
Refunds up to ₦20,000 need one person; above that, a second person confirms.
For a dispute, attach the receipt, the scan or vote record, and the terms version accepted.

articles.title: Payouts and holds
articles.sum: Partners and referrers are paid on Fridays. A changed bank account holds the payout for a check.
blocks: A payout is held when bank details changed in the last 7 days, until someone confirms the change with the account owner by phone.
Payout runs Friday. Anything ready by Thursday 18:00 goes in it.
Each partner sees what’s coming in their own area.

articles.title: Access that ends on its own
articles.sum: Every access given for one event or award has an end date. Nobody has to remember to remove it.
blocks: Event leads and teams: the day after the event.
Moderators on an award: when you set it, often after results.
Volunteers: each role ends with its award or event.
Expired access removes the place from the person’s menu on their next request.

articles.title: Volunteers
articles.sum: Volunteers work from their own area, never this console. What they check shows here as a recommendation with their name.
blocks: Green or red at their gate
Most hours log themselves: door scans, accepted checks and verified sign-ups. Volunteers log by hand only for work nobody saw; their lead confirms it.
Volunteers never see an /admin page or link.
Data is masked on the server. Hiding it on screen isn’t masking.
Retention is a second shift. Thank people by name within a day of their first one.

articles.title: Judges
articles.sum: Judges have their own area. They declare conflicts before they see finalists.
blocks: Invite from the edition’s Judging › Panels.
A judge with no reply after 3 days gets one reminder; after that, call them.
A declared conflict removes them from that category’s scorecards.

articles.title: Broadcasts and quiet hours
articles.sum: Only opted-in people, never between 21:00 and 08:00, and the SMS cost is shown before you send.
blocks: A segment of opted-in people. The count updates as you go.
Email is free. SMS shows its cost; a big SMS send is a request to comms.
Quiet hours (21:00 to 08:00) are skipped automatically.
Nobody is messaged without opting in to that channel.
SMS spend over ₦50,000 a day pauses sends and tells finance.

articles.title: Letters
articles.sum: Finalist, sponsor and reference letters merge from records and are signed by the named person.
blocks: The finalist letter includes how voting works, from the edition’s own rules.
Sponsor letters merge the tier and the benefits owed.
Volunteer reference letters list only verified hours and roles.
Preview with one real record before sending to all.

articles.title: What we never say in public
articles.sum: A short list of words and claims that never appear on a public page, email or letter.
blocks: Never mention AI in public. Gee is just the name of our helper.
Never describe voting in shopping language: no buy, cart, checkout or price.
Never show the same fact twice on one screen.

articles.title: Moderation
articles.sum: Comments, messages and quotes stay hidden until a person looks. Reports from several people go first.
blocks: Hide the detail, publish the rest
Remove and flag the nominee’s page

articles.title: Alert levels
articles.sum: Affects production means people are being failed now. May affect production means they will be if nobody acts.
blocks: Red count on the bell, red pill in the header
Every alert says what to do next and links to the page that fixes it.

articles.title: Playbook: payments not recorded
articles.sum: The gateway takes money, the webhook answers, and nothing is written. Stop new losses, then fix each payment.
blocks: Gateway check shows payments with no vote, ticket or receipt.
Settings › Payments: make the fallback provider primary while you investigate.
Pin a reply to tickets that mention a missing vote.
Oldest first. Each one creates what was paid for, once.
Add a decision to the audit log with cause and fix.
Don’t ask people to pay again. Reconciling makes their payment count.

articles.title: Playbook: backups and the restore drill
articles.sum: A backup you’ve never restored isn’t a backup. Run the drill every quarter.
blocks: Today nothing backs up the database. One copy on one machine. This is the top risk on Alerts.
Set up a nightly backup off the machine
Settings › Security and sign-in › Database backup.
Every quarter, restore last night’s backup into the sandbox.
A recent vote, a recent payment and a recent nomination exist.

articles.title: Privacy and data
articles.sum: Collect what a task needs, mask it on the server, and keep it only as long as the retention window.
blocks: Phone numbers show as 0803 ••• ••12 to anyone who doesn’t need them.
ID photos for door, money and data roles are deleted after the check.
Anyone can download their data from their account.
Retention windows aren’t set yet, so erasure can’t run. This needs a decision in Settings › Legal.
Masking happens on the server. Hiding data in the page isn’t masking.

articles.title: The audit log and evidence
articles.sum: Every change is logged with who, when and why. Entries and reviewed evidence can’t be edited.
blocks: Evidence is immutable once reviewed. There is no edit or delete for it.
Audit entries can’t be edited or deleted. A correction is a new entry.
Add a note when you act. It’s the only place the why is kept.
